title: Some Antidepressants May Work Better Than Others Long Term - Nautilus
gist: A Lancet Psychiatry review found escitalopram (Lexapro), duloxetine (Cymbalta) and agomelatine (Valdoxan) linked to better long-term symptom improvement than fluoxetine (Prozac), with Lexapro and Cymbalta users also more likely to stay on medication; the authors question whether that makes them 'best'.

insights.claim: A review in The Lancet Psychiatry found people taking escitalopram (Lexapro), duloxetine (Cymbalta) and agomelatine (Valdoxan) were more likely to report improved depression symptoms over the long term than those taking fluoxetine (Prozac).
insights.so_what: Comparative-effectiveness evidence could shift prescribing share among generic antidepressants.
insights.locator: The research, published in The Lancet
insights.speaker: Lauren Cortis

insights.claim: Patients on Lexapro and Cymbalta were also more likely to stay on their medications than those on Prozac, per the Lancet Psychiatry review.
insights.so_what: Adherence is a key driver of real-world outcomes and prescription volume.
insights.quote: For those taking Lexapro and Cymbalta, they were also more likely to stay on their medications.
insights.locator: The research, published in The Lancet
insights.speaker: Lauren Cortis

insights.claim: The authors caution against concluding that these drugs are simply the 'best' antidepressants, signaling caveats to the review's findings.
insights.so_what: Don't over-read single reviews as a durable prescribing shift.
insights.quote: But does that mean these are the best antidepressants?
insights.speaker: Lauren Cortis
